title: Stop returning a hardcoded default from build() in the 5 notification preference providers (SM-2)

evidence.quote:
_loadFromPrefs(profileId);
    return true; // synchronous default; overwritten once prefs load completes

_loadFromPrefs(profileId);
    return true; // synchronous default; overwritten once prefs load completes

_loadFromPrefs(profileId);
    return true; // synchronous default; overwritten once prefs load completes

// reminderEnabledProvider returns the default `true` synchronously and
      // then async-loads the persisted `false`. That state change invalidates

// M3 fix: the pref notifiers return defaults (enabled=true, 19:00)
  // synchronously, then async-load the real values.

final enabled = ref.watch(streakAlertEnabledProvider);
  final time = ref.watch(streakAlertTimeProvider);

why: ReminderEnabled, ReminderTime, StreakAlertEnabled, StreakAlertTime and RewardNotificationEnabled all fire an async SharedPreferences load from build() and return a hardcoded default first. reminder_sync_sacred_time_test.dart's own comment documents the real consequence: this oscillation 'invalidates this effect mid-flight, disposing the first in-flight future (Riverpod throws "disposed during loading")' for any dependent FutureProvider whenever the persisted value differs from the default -- the test only passes by retrying up to 10 times. The M3 fix (lines 463-467) patches only reminderSyncEffect's symptom by re-reading SharedPreferences directly; the root defect reaches every other consumer (UI switches, streakAlertSyncEffect, future code) unmitigated.
recommendation: Convert these 5 providers to AsyncNotifier<T> (or an equivalent that actually awaits SharedPreferences before emitting) so there is no synchronous-default race; then delete the M3 workaround in reminderSyncEffect.
acceptance_criteria: A unit test asserts reminderEnabledProvider (and siblings) never emits the hardcoded default when a differing persisted value exists for the resolved profile.
reminder_sync_sacred_time_test.dart's retry-loop workaround (lines 265-274) is deleted once the fix lands and the test still passes on the first attempt.
mergedFrom: Give streakAlertSyncEffect the same cold-start defense and test coverage as reminderSyncEffect
